artifacts.summary: Guarded subagent-postflight.sh's block-reason extraction and events-log-lifecycle.sh's SubagentStop telemetry with jq empty parse-validity checks, added deviation-event logging for the malformed-marker case, a registered 9-case regression suite, and documented the hook-idiom survey plus the two hooks' intentional divergence.

completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed the malformed-postflight-marker defect: subagent-postflight.sh now emits a diagnostic block reason naming the marker path and jq's parse error instead of an empty string, events-log-lifecycle.sh now logs exactly one deviation event for the same malformed marker instead of silently exiting, both changes covered by a new 9-case registered regression suite, and the 51 other jq // idiom sites documented as tolerant-by-design in postflight-control.md.

memory_candidates.content: jq's `//` alternative operator only fires on an absent/null field, never on a JSON parse error. An unguarded `jq -r '.field // "non-empty default"' "$FILE" 2>/dev/null` silently collapses 'file has no .field' and 'file does not parse as JSON at all' into the same default, with 2>/dev/null also swallowing jq's own diagnostic. Fix: precede with `jq empty "$FILE"` and branch the parse-failure case separately. `// empty` (or `// ""` where the caller treats empty as a no-op) is safe unguarded since both cases collapse to identical caller behavior anyway -- only a non-empty, semantically load-bearing default needs the guard.

In this repo, scripts/events-append.sh (and other core scripts sourcing lib/common.sh's common_repo_root) resolve their write root via a fixed script-path depth from their OWN location, not from the caller's cwd -- and deploy-root-guard.sh additionally refuses to run at all when the immediate parent directory isn't literally named .claude or .opencode (rejects source-store invocation outright). A test that needs to drive such a script in isolation must copy the script (and its sibling scripts/lib deps) into a fresh <tmp>/.claude/{hooks,scripts,scripts/lib}/ tree with <tmp>/specs/ as a sibling, rather than invoking the real hooks/scripts in place -- otherwise it either hard-fails (source-store) or silently writes test rows into the real repo's specs/events.jsonl (deployed).
